name: Chinese ink painting
material: carbon-based ink on absorbent paper or silk; may be monochrome or combined with restrained color
fabrication_process: load brush with controlled water/ink concentration
build calligraphic lines, washes, texture strokes and blank-space relationships
visible_production_marks: tonal density from pale gray to saturated black
edge_behavior: Edges vary by brush speed, moisture and absorbency: decisive calligraphic contours can coexist with dissolved wash edges.
mark_making: tonal density from pale gray to saturated black
color_behavior: Value comes from ink concentration and water; blank substrate is an active light/color field.
surface_behavior: Absorbent fibers/silk weave subtly affect stroke edges; no thick acrylic impasto.
composition_behavior: Use spatial rhythm, void, directional brushwork and selective detail instead of photographic depth-of-field simulation.
structural_limitations: do not render every surface with equal microdetail
avoid Western watercolor blooms as the only ink behavior
aging_weathering: paper may fox/yellow/crease depending on state
mounting wear and seals/inscriptions only when appropriate and verified

prompt_fragments.core: Reconstruct the subject with calligraphic brush line, controlled ink dilution, dry/wet stroke contrast and meaningful untouched paper/silk; let brush rhythm describe form rather than tracing a photo under a filter.

sources.supports: ink tone, saturation, line, brushwork and texture as critical distinctions
calligraphic brush line and ink-on-paper scholar painting traditions

scope_note: This module controls material/production behavior. It does not select an era by itself.
